title: ProxySQL — Connection Pool & Routing
description: ProxySQL built-in Prometheus exporter (:6070). Pool = backend connections shared by all app clients (multiplexing).

panels.title: Backend status
panels.description: Status of each MySQL backend as seen by ProxySQL.

panels.title: Client connections created / aborted per sec
Waiting clients (delayed / failed backend-connection requests per sec)
panels.description: ProxySQL has no 'queue length' metric. These two counters rise when clients had to wait for (or could not get) a backend connection — i.e. the pool is saturated.

targets.legendFormat: pool could not provide a connection

panels.title: Pool utilization
panels.description: used / (used + free) connections currently open to MySQL.

panels.title: Multiplexing efficiency
panels.description: High reuse + many clients per backend connection = pooling is doing its job.

panels.title: Connections opened to MySQL per sec
Avg backend query latency
panels.description: Time ProxySQL spent talking to MySQL, per query. ProxySQL exports totals, not histograms, so percentiles are not available — see the MySQL dashboard for statement latency.

options.content: **Transaction latency:** ProxySQL's Prometheus exporter does not expose per-transaction duration. Use *Avg backend query latency* together with *Active transactions* above, and application-side spans in Tempo (`order.place`, JDBC spans) for end-to-end transaction timing.

panels.title: Server login failures
panels.description: Failed attempts to log in to MySQL backends (wrong credentials / unreachable) plus failed client logins to ProxySQL.
